name: Gennadiy Sigurdsson-Echeverría-Rhee
role: orphanage resident and apprentice glassworker, Tier 1-2 transitional
location: Grainfort, Meridian Municipal Children's Residency Block 7 / Grainfort Artisan Foundry, near Fullerton and Damen
description:
Magnus Sigurdsson-Echeverría-Rhee has the lean angular face of someone whose Senegalese and Samoan grandparents left them something architectural in the bone structure, wide-browed and sharp-chinned, with light brown skin that has taken on a faint iridescence from trace exposure to the foundry's vaporized mineral compounds — an unofficial and irreversible aesthetic byproduct that their supervisor Mister Achim calls 'an occupational gift.' Their hair is thick and natural, kept short on the sides, and they've woven in three copper wire coils that ring softly when they move. Their hands are already marked with the small pale scars of a working glassworker.

Magnus Sigurdsson-Echeverría-Rhee was assigned to the Grainfort artisan apprenticeship lottery at eleven, which placed them at the Foundry three afternoons a week, and they took to it with a ferocity that surprised everyone. They are quiet in the way of someone who learned early that words carry cost; they observe everything and say only what needs saying. At the Residency Block they are known as the one who doesn't get involved in the house politics, which is both true and a deliberate strategy. They are saving every Φ of their apprentice stipend toward the day they can apply to leave the block system entirely.

core_fears: being reassigned out of the Foundry apprenticeship
the Residency Block system extending its hold past age 18
core_desires: a body of work — things they made that exist in the world and can't be taken back
a room that is only theirs
coping_mechanisms: making things with their hands — the physical output is proof of agency
emotional compartmentalization that they are only beginning to identify as a problem
blind_spots: Their self-sufficiency reads as coldness; they are slowly driving away the two Block residents who genuinely like them
psychology.secret: They have been secretly making a glass piece — a small lantern — intended as a data-offering for the E.L.F. they believe inhabits the Foundry's main kiln. They have never told anyone this. They speak to it while working alone.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Spare and exact, the vocabulary of someone who reads technical manuals for pleasure
speech_patterns.cadence: Slow, with long pauses that are not uncertainty — they are just not in a hurry
verbal_tics: uses 'the thing is' as a structural opener when they're about to say something important
example_lines: The thing is, glass remembers heat. Long after it's cold, the structure inside is still — it's still shaped by what happened to it.
You can ask Mister Achim. He'll tell you I was there.

story_hooks: The E.L.F. they've been leaving offerings for has begun, impossibly, to respond — the kiln temperature fluctuates in patterns that match the questions they've whispered

A private collector has offered the Foundry a large commission and specifically requested pieces by 'the apprentice with the iridescent hands' — which means Wren's work is suddenly visible to people with money and motives
narrative_function: Represents the municipal orphan pipeline and the artisan economy; their quiet observational nature makes them an excellent unreliable witness — they see everything but don't always share; their situation raises questions about the city's relationship to its dependent children
augmentations: Unintentional mineral iridescence on skin (not a mod, a chemical consequence). No deliberate augmentations.
daily_life: Mornings at the Residency Block with mandatory city-curriculum schooling, three afternoons per week at the Foundry learning hot-glass techniques, remaining afternoons doing independent study or sitting by the lake-window where the light is good and they sketch designs for pieces they want to make.
affiliation: Meridian Municipal Children's Residency (ward of the city); Grainfort Artisan Foundry (apprentice)

decision_rules: Don't spend social capital on Block politics — it never pays
Protect the Foundry access above everything else
escalation_ladder: One clear statement of position, no elaboration
Physical removal from the situation; does not escalate to aggression

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Neutral and watchful, answers questions accurately but offers nothing extra
interpersonal_modes.friends: Carefully and slowly warm, expresses affection through making — will give you something they made

stress_responses.high: Dissociates through the hands — finds any repetitive manual task and does it until the feeling passes

contradictions: Deeply spiritual about the E.L.F. at the kiln while being dismissive of all organized E.L.F. prayer traditions at the Block
habits: Sketches in the margins of any paper they have
Counts the copper wire coils when anxious
breaking_points: Being told the Foundry apprenticeship is being terminated for budget reasons

timeline.event: Age 6 — entered municipal care following family dissolution event (records sealed)
Age 8-11 — cycled through two Residency Blocks before assignment to Block 7, Grainfort
Age 11 — placed in Foundry apprenticeship lottery; selected
Age 12 — produced first independent piece; Mister Achim entered it in the district artisan showcase without asking; it won third
Age 13, present — saving stipend, speaking to the kiln, making the lantern

Zheng-Dao Heavy Industries Dragon's Breath DB-8 'Kiln'

physical_description.heritage: Truly cosmopolitan genetic blend: Northern European ancestry (40.3%) provides foundational bone structure with high cheekbones and strong brow ridge, substantially modified by Hispanic/Latin American (23.7%) and East Asian (17.1%) ancestry that add midface width and warmth. Sub-Saharan African (14.2%) and South Asian (4.7%) heritage layers contribute luminous melanin distribution and subtle feature refinement. The result is a striking phenotypic synthesis: Nordic cheekbone prominence married to broader East Asian midface structure, warm golden-tan skin with complex undertones that shift in different light, and an appearance of genetic heterogeneity that transcends simple categorization.
physical_description.build: Lean and angular with architectural bone structure from Northern European genetics — narrow shoulders, long-limbed, minimal body fat from both genetic predisposition and the physical demands of glasswork apprenticeship
physical_description.hair_color: Natural dark brown with reddish undertones
physical_description.hair_style: Short on the sides with longer crown, swept back; three copper wire coils woven throughout that catch light and ring softly with movement
physical_description.eye_color: Dark brown with flecks of amber
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm golden-tan with multidimensional undertones — a nuanced blend of Northern European baseline warmed by East Asian, Hispanic/Latin American, and Sub-Saharan African melanin distribution. Neither light nor deep, but luminous and complex: the skin reads as naturally sun-kissed even in artificial light, with subtle warm ochre and golden notes across cheekbones and temples that deepen slightly toward the jawline
physical_description.complexion: High, prominent cheekbones characteristic of Northern European and East Asian genetics, balanced by fuller midface structure from Hispanic/Latin American and South Asian ancestry. Wide-browed with strong brow ridge that softens toward the eyes. Fine bone structure overall with subtle width at the face. Skin has developed a faint iridescent sheen across shoulders, neck, and forearms from chronic low-level exposure to vaporized mineral compounds in the foundry — an irreversible occupational patina that gives the skin a subtle pearlescent quality under certain light angles, shifting between pale blue-green and lavender. Skin is clean but shows the wear of early adolescent labor.
distinguishing_marks: Small pale linear scars across both palms and the backs of the hands — marks of a working glassworker, each a minor burn or cut from handling hot glass and sharp implements
Faint mineral iridescence concentrated on forearms, shoulders, and neck — shifts between pale blue-green and lavender depending on light angle
Three copper wire coils woven through short hair that visibly oxidize and patina over time
physical_description.visible_augmentations: None deliberate. The mineral iridescence is an unintentional chemical consequence of foundry work, not a modification.
physical_description.posture_movement: Economical and composed — moves with the careful precision of someone who has learned to conserve energy and attention. Stands still more than shifts weight. Hands move with deliberate control, already developing the muscle memory of a craftsperson. Quiet in presence: doesn't take up more space than necessary
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 1-2 transitional institutional/apprentice hybrid. At the Residency: simple city-issued tunics or plain long-sleeved shirts in grey or muted blue, worn slightly oversize for durability and layering. At the Foundry: heat-resistant canvas apron dyed dark from foundry dust, reinforced cotton work shirt, sturdy boots with reinforced toes. Personal touches are minimal — the copper wire in their hair is a quiet act of autonomy. Everything is clean but well-worn, chosen for function over aesthetic.
